summary: The terminal interface opens documents: by name in Ctrl+K, from the documents list, from a doc/ link in a message, a mission or a document, and from the documents a mission and its steps name

schema.detail: No database schema, version or stored data changes.

rules.detail: No checkpoint rules or coordination changes; no coordinated upgrade required.

compatibility.detail: The daemon's client API now passes two error codes through instead of internal: document-not-synced (a pinned version that has not reached this host yet) and invalid-document-reference. Both were already declared in the client contract, and the Rust, Swift and TypeScript clients already recognize them, so older clients keep working; a client tells not-synced apart from internal only against an updated daemon (upgrade daemons before relying on it). The terminal interface reads documents through the existing client routes (document.get, documents.list, document-references.get) and the shared document view model; the document pane it already had for st ui open doc/NAME@HASH keeps its key and now renders through that model, so bytes that are not UTF-8 say so instead of being shown with replacement characters. Against a daemon without the documents capability, a document read by a bare name or the list says why it could not be read.
